validity.researcher_notes: RETRACTED 2026-07-28 and kept only as provenance. This record concluded that P4067 is a crude-oil line misfiled in GGIT, reasoning from Al-Ahdab being a CRUDE-OIL FIELD (the same conclusion docs/country_notes/iraq.md carried from the 2026-07-07 harvest). The inference is invalid: an oil field produces associated gas, and this line's destination is a POWER STATION ('Al-Zubaydia PWR St') -- a gas line from an oil field to a power plant is the most ordinary object in Iraq's gas network (Majnoon, Gharraf, Faiha, West Qurna and Buzergan rows are all that shape). Reading BOTH ASB2017 tables side by side settles it: OPEC lists the corridor's gas line in Table 9.9 ('Al-Ahdeb/Al-Zubaydia PWR St, OPC, 73, 16' = this row) and its crude lines separately in Table 6.9 ('Ahdeb/Wassit P P (2), OPC, 42, 45, 16, 10'), so it distinguished them deliberately -- the opposite of a misfiling. See the qc leg's record for the full ruling and notes/escalation-2026-07-28-iraq-gasoil-misfiled.md for the general rule this violated: key on what the source says the pipe CARRIES, never on what its origin field produces. ORIGINAL TEXT of this record, preserved verbatim for provenance: The pipe physically EXISTS (not a phantom), but GEM's Fuel=Gas classification is not supported by any independent source and appears wrong. GEM's own cited sources are all about the Al-Ahdab OIL field (BBC Arabic 2011 on Ahdab oil production start; Iraq Business News Ahdab field page; OPEC ASB 2017 p.134) — none describes a GAS pipeline. Independent sources uniformly describe the Al-Ahdab -> Zubaidiya feeder as a CRUDE OIL pipeline: (1) Al-Sharq (Iraqi press quoting the State Company for Oil Projects/SCOP) calls the project 'مشروع مد أنبوب النفط الخام المغذي لمحطة كهرباء الزبيدية – الأحدب' (the crude-oil feeder pipeline for Zubaidiya power station), completed at 76 km, delivered via two crude-oil pumping stations at Al-Ahdab and a receiving station at Zubaidiya. (2) MEES (2023) states Zubaidiya is an 'oil-fired power plant' supplied with crude oil (e.g. 24,000 b/d from Gharaf), not gas. (3) China.org.cn (Arabic, CNPC BRI feature) says the Al-Ahdab project 'يوفر الوقود لمحطة كهرباء الزبيدية' (supplies fuel to Zubaidiya, Iraq's largest power plant). The Al-Ahdab field's associated gas is processed to LPG for domestic distribution in Wasit, not piped as fuel gas to the plant. Endpoints (Al-Ahdab field -> Al-Zubaydia, Wasit), owner (Iraq Ministry of Oil), and FuelSource=Al-Ahdab all fit a crude line. Conclusion: real pipe, but it is a crude-oil power-station feeder mislabeled as a gas transmission trunk. Tier high: >=2 independent origins (SCOP/Iraqi press, MEES, China.org.cn) agree it is crude-oil / an oil-fired plant.

validity.researcher_notes: GEM lists LengthKnown=73.00 mi (= ~117 km). Independent sources give the built Al-Ahdab -> Zubaidiya feeder as 76 km (Al-Sharq / SCOP: 'مد الأنبوب بطول 76 كم') and ~75 km (English trade-press descriptions of the same project). The GEM figure of 73 matches 75-76 km far better as KILOMETRES than as miles, so the 'mi' unit tag is likely wrong (should be ~75-76 km / ~47 mi). Flagging as a spec/units conflict rather than silently passing. Diameter (16 in) and Capacity (blank) could not be independently corroborated and are moot pending the reclassification to a crude line. REFINED 2026-07-28: this record's phrasing ('real line is ~75-76 km') could be misread as an instruction to overwrite 73 with 75. It is not. 73 is already the ASB figure in KILOMETRES; the defect is only the 'mi' unit label, which makes the computed LengthKnownKm 117.48. The one-cell fix is the unit label alone -- see notes/escalation-2026-07-28-asb-iraq-length-units.md and the asb-length-units leg's record, which is the authoritative form of this edit. Al-Jibawi's independent 76 km for the corridor corroborates the km reading.

routes.start_name: Al-Ahdab (Al-Ahdeb) oil field, Wasit province (~27 km west of Kut, ~180 km SE of Baghdad)
routes.corridor_desc: Runs entirely within Wasit province, NW from the Al-Ahdab oil field (Al-Ahrar/Al-Ahdeb area west of Kut) to the Zubaidiya thermal power station north of Kut. Straight-line separation between the two sourced points is ~65 km, consistent with a routed ~75-76 km pipeline. Corridor bound is moderately tight (both endpoints are named, sourced facilities within one province) but the intermediate alignment is unsourced, so treat as a corridor, not a traced route. Note: the built line uses two crude pump stations at Al-Ahdab and a receiving station at Zubaidiya.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from sourced named facilities: Al-Ahdab field centroid ~32.424N,45.714E (field bounding box 45°30'-45°46'E / 32°23'-32°35'N per remote-sensing lit; ~27 km west of Kut per Arabic press); Zubaidiya power plant ~32.7736N,45.0826E (published plant coordinate). Coordinates are approximate facility points, not surveyed pipe vertices; no coordinates were invented. Al-Sharq/SCOP names the crude pump stations at Al-Ahdab and the receiving station at Zubaidiya; those station points are not individually geolocated so no waypoint coords are asserted.

summary: P4067 is a real pipe but MISCLASSIFIED: it is the Al-Ahdab->Zubaidiya CRUDE-OIL power-station feeder (~75-76 km, oil-fired plant, SCOP), not a gas transmission line; also a length/units conflict (73 'mi' vs sourced ~76 km).
